column1: # Product-name occurrences inside the six copied trees (`lisp`, `test`, `etc`, `doc`,
# `leim`, `admin` -> `femacs/<top>/**`), one per line.  PORTING.md 0.1-19 says those trees are
# copied, and `tools/check-verbatim.py` holds them byte for byte; the tenth half of the rule
# (status 3.613, 2026-10-05) is the one exception: a *string the reference program prints* that
# names the reference product as this program's own name, welcome, warranty line or generated-file
# identity is this program's outward identity, so it carries this repository's name instead.
# The rule is mechanical - the token is replaced and nothing else on the line changes - and every
# row is read by the gate: the target's line must be exactly the text below, the reference's line
# must differ from it, and a row for a file the copy does not carry, or a difference with no row,
# is a failure.  Columns: <repo-relative target path>\t<line>\t<the target's line>\t<reason>.

column3: the target's line
column4: reason

column3: (format "femacs %s (build %s, %s%s%s%s)%s"

column1: # 0.1-19's eleventh half (status 3.632, 2026-10-06): the copied trees' own membership declaration,
# `This file is part of GNU Emacs.` - a statement about *the file* that names the reference product as
# its owner.  Each site below writes this repository's name instead, in the tenth half's mechanical
# form (only the product token changes; the rest of the line is untouched), so every file stays
# line-for-line identical otherwise.  Three of them are *generators* - they write that sentence into
# 355, `cedet/semantic/bovine/grammar.el` 493) - and eight are the program's own buffer names
# (`*GNU Emacs*` / `*About GNU Emacs*`), i.e. names the program itself writes; both shapes are the
# tenth half's criterion.  `test/` is not in this list: the goal text forbids modifying test files.
# A `ChangeLog*` is not either: those quote the sentence as history, not as a declaration.
